jobs.name: word_count
jobs.title: Word count over track titles
jobs.objective: Implement the canonical MapReduce word count on real text
pipeline: combine(word, [1,1,..]) -> sum  (runs inside each map task)
jobs.note: Stopwords and tokens shorter than 3 characters are filtered during the map phase.

jobs.name: aggregates
jobs.title: Per-decade aggregates over danceability, energy, valence, tempo
jobs.objective: MapReduce aggregates (sum + count -> mean) with a combiner
pipeline: combine(decade, tuples) -> element-wise sum  (combiner shrinks the shuffle)
jobs.note: The combiner is what makes this scalable: only one tuple per decade per map task crosses the network.

jobs.name: join
jobs.title: Map-side join: tracks joined with the cluster label table
jobs.objective: Join a large relation (tracks) with a small one (cluster labels)
pipeline: broadcast the 5-row cluster->label table to every map task
map(track) -> [(label, 1)] for matched rows (inner join semantics)
combine + reduce -> count of tracks per acoustic profile
jobs.note: Broadcast table: 5 rows. A map-side join avoids shuffling the 25,000-row left side.

jobs.name: top_n
jobs.title: Sorting: top 15 artists by track count
jobs.objective: MapReduce counting + sort for top-N reporting
pipeline: combine + reduce -> total tracks per artist
sort the reduced output descending and cut the top N
jobs.note: Split on ';' / ',' so multi-artist credits each get a vote.

jobs.name: inverted_index
jobs.title: Searching: inverted index (token -> posting list)
jobs.objective: Build a searchable index without scanning every row per query
pipeline: map(track) -> [(token, track_id)] for every title token
combine(token, ids) -> first 8 postings (bounded, like a real posting cap)
jobs.note: An index turns an O(n) scan per query into one lookup - the same idea as the Bloom pre-filter in Exp.6.

concepts: bit array of m bits + k independent hash functions
double hashing h_i = (h1 + i*h2) mod m
false positives possible, false negatives impossible
optimal sizing m = -n ln p / (ln 2)^2, k = (m/n) ln 2
